newsitem.title: UK: EMS/Mark shaky vs crosses in late Europe.
newsitem.headline: EMS/Mark shaky vs crosses in late Europe.

text.p: The mark was shaky against its crosses in late Europe, largely unimpressed by strong German jobless and industry figures which failed to provide any lingering support.
Traders said a runaway dollar/mark, which soared to a fresh 34-month high of 1.7210, took the shine off any mark gains.
The German February jobless figure, while stronger than anticipated, also had its pitfalls and could not hide the fact that German labour markets remain weak, said analysts.

"It's going to take a succession of strong numbers now for the market to really start believing the German economy is picking up," said Jeremy Hawkins, chief economic adviser at Bank of America in London.
German February unemployment, up a seasonally adjusted 5,000 to 4.316 million, was lower than forecasts for a 20,000 rise.
The unadjusted figure at 4.672 million was bang in line with forecasts for a 12.2 percent rise and leaks.
"The improved weather in February has encouraged construction firms to start re-hiring workers," said David Brickman, European economist at Yamaichi International.
